item.title: Leopard kills zookeeper
item.description: A keeper at a Dutch zoo has died days after being mauled in a leopard enclosure, the safari park announced on Tuesday. The woman was attacked while caring for two Persian leopards in an indoor facility at the Beekse Bergen park in the south of the Netherlands. It is not clear exactly what happened in the enclosure as there are no cameras. The animals were inside due to bad weather and staff are usually kept away from the leopards. She sustained serious injuries to her head and neck, according to local media. She underwent emergency surgery but died on Tuesday, the zoo said in a statement. “The keeper started at the Beekse Bergen Safari Park at the age of 17 and worked here, with only a few short interruptions, for nearly 40 years,” the statement said. An independent investigation will be launched to establish the circumstances of the incident, the zoo added. The leopards were behaving naturally, a park spokesperson told Omroep Brabant, a local media outlet. “They are, and remain, predators.” Vanguard News The post Leopard kills zookeeper appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: DSS tenders firearms used during kidnap of NYSC members
item.description: By Chidi Nkwopara, Owerri The Department of State Service (DSS) on Tuesday tendered the firearms allegedly used during the kidnap of 20 prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), members travelling to their orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom States. The exhibits included three AK 47 rifles, four AK 47 magazines, 81 live 7.62mm ammunition and one unbranded and unregistered English-made pistol. Disclosing this when he was led in evidence by the Principal State Counsel, Mr Ekezie Nwauzor, the first prosecution witness, PW1, Mr Ikechukwu Emmanuel, gave a graphic account of how the first defendant, Usman Aliyu, took security personnel into a bush where the guns were recovered. He said that during the investigation, Usman Aliyu led security operatives to a thick bush around Okuku, Owerri West local council area of Imo State, where the exhibits were concealed in a polythene bag and buried. Continuing, the PW1 said that while the recovered exhibits were brought back to the DSS Office in Owerri, the three accused persons confirmed that all the recovered items were used during the kidnapping of the 20 NYSC members on October 1, 2026. Answering another question, the PW1 said that a total sum of N48 million was paid as ransom by the relatives of the kidnapped victims, adding that N47 million was paid in dollars, while N1 million was paid in naira. He equally told the court that Usman Aliyu confirmed during interrogation that the dollars were later changed to naira, but only the sum of N155,200 was recovered from the three accused persons at the point of arrest. The court ordered that all the recovered firearms, live ammunition and cash be kept in the custody of the Armourer, DSS State Command, Owerri. Hearing in the suit, HOU/22C/2026, continues today, Wednesday, October 28, 2026. The post DSS tenders firearms used during kidnap of NYSC members appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: JIBWIS disowns AK-47 threat against non-Muslims in Plateau, Enugu
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – The Jama’atu Izalatil Bid’a Wa’ikamatis Sunnah (JIBWIS) has dissociated itself from a viral video in which some persons described as aides of the group allegedly called for the use of AK-47 rifles to attack non-Muslims in Plateau and Enugu states. The video, which emerged on social media on Monday, had generated widespread condemnation, with calls for the arrest and prosecution of those featured in it. In a statement issued at the group’s headquarters in Jos on Tuesday, the National Publicity Secretary of JIBWIS, Sheikh Ahmad Muhammad Ashiru, said, “Though we are yet to substantiate the authenticity of the video, JIBWIS will not support any call to attack or kill any human being.” He said, “JIBWIS, under the leadership of Ash-Sheikh Muhammad Sani Yahaya Jingir, denounces calls to violence under any guise, especially now that households are trying to endure the pains of insecurity in the form of banditry, kidnapping, armed robbery and Boko Haram in the North-West, North-Central, North-East and other parts of the country.” Ashiru said, “We would not support any call capable of disturbing the peace of Nigeria, as such comments are capable of inciting violence and creating unnecessary tension among Nigerians.” He added, “Whoever does that in the name of the group does so at his own peril and will not be accepted by the organisation.” The JIBWIS spokesman said, “Such comments do not represent Islamic teachings, and the organisation remains committed to peace, peaceful coexistence and respect for the sanctity of human life.” He called on the security agencies to urgently investigate the video, saying, “We call on security agencies to carry out their duty with due diligence and bring the culprit to justice.” Ashiru stressed that anyone found culpable after investigation should be dealt with according to the law, saying, “We believe that the appropriate authorities have the responsibility to establish the authenticity of the video, identify those involved and take necessary action.” The post JIBWIS disowns AK-47 threat against non-Muslims in Plateau, Enugu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Chelsea’s Joao Pedro ruled out with thigh injury
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Chelsea have suffered an injury setback ahead of their Carabao Cup clash against Liverpool on Wednesday, with forward Joao Pedro expected to be sidelined for “a few weeks” with a thigh injury, head coach Xabi Alonso has confirmed. Speaking ahead of the trip to Liverpool, Alonso said the Brazilian was not ready for the upcoming matches after sustaining the injury that ruled him out of Chelsea’s defeat to Tottenham. “Injury on his thigh – he’s going to be a few weeks out. How many? We don’t want to predict. He’s not ready for the next games,” Alonso said, according to Sky Sports. The Chelsea manager described Joao Pedro as a key player but insisted his side had enough depth to cope with his absence as they prepare for a demanding run of fixtures. “He’s a key player. We will miss him. We will be ready to deal with that and be ready to win games with the players we have available starting against Liverpool. We are ready to fight and show a good level,” he added. Alonso stressed that building a strong squad meant having alternatives available when key players were injured, urging his team to focus on solutions rather than setbacks. “This is why you build a squad. Yes, players are important but you need to build a squad. You look for solutions rather than excuses,” he said. Alonso: Palmer knows he made a mistake Meanwhile, Alonso said Cole Palmer understood his error after being sent off against Tottenham, a dismissal that rules the England international out of the Liverpool trip through suspension. The Chelsea boss said he had spoken with Palmer and believed the midfielder recognised that the incident could have been avoided. “We spoke and for sure he knows the mistake he made. Things that you can avoid. I hope that this is not going to be repeated. He’s aware of that, he’s mature and it was a mistake,” Alonso said. Despite the suspension, Alonso expressed confidence in Palmer’s relationship with his teammates, saying the club wanted him to remain happy and enjoy his football. “He’s in a good space, he connects very well socially with his teammates. They like him, they want Cole smiling, they want Cole having fun, enjoying his game because when we see that, he’ll have a better team,” he added. item.title: 2027: My ambition driven by desire to uplift common man – Ex-IGP Adamu
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia Former Inspector-General of Police, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, has said his ambition to become Nasarawa State governor in 2027 is driven by a desire to improve the lives of ordinary citizens. Adamu stated this on Tuesday in Doma while reacting to his endorsement by the Alago nation as its preferred governorship candidate for the 2027 election. The endorsement was announced at a rally organised by the Alago Support Group for IGP Adamu. The former police chief, who is seeking the governorship on the platform of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), said his decision to contest was motivated by concerns over the welfare of ordinary people, particularly women, children and youths. “Our coming out for this election is for the common people. We came out for the common man, to see that the common man does not suffer the way they are suffering now,” he said. Adamu expressed appreciation to the support group for its endorsement and willingness to work with his campaign. He also expressed optimism about his chances of winning the election. He thanked God for the progress recorded in his political journey and pledged to prioritise education, healthcare and security if elected governor. “We will put people’s lives first, to see that education with quality is given to our people, health with quality our people have obtained, and the issue of security, we will see that everyone will find peace, so that people can return to their homes to sleep without any fear,” he said. Adamu also raised concerns over alleged vote-buying and the collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) from women, warning that such practices could discourage eligible voters from participating in the election. “Those who don’t have people following them are collecting cards in the hands of women, they are buying so as to stop them from coming out to vote,” he said. He urged anyone whose PVC had been collected to retrieve it and encouraged residents not to sell their cards but to come out and vote on election day. Earlier, the leader of the conveners, Danjuma Joseph, said the movement was established because the Alago people wanted to play an active role in determining the political future of Nasarawa State. Joseph said the group had assessed Adamu’s record and considered him a candidate with integrity, patriotism and a history of service to Nigeria. He added that Adamu had longstanding ties to the Alago community, noting that he had attended school with prominent sons and daughters of the area in Obi and had maternal connections to the people. “We have resolved that we will no longer be onlookers or fence-sitters while the political destiny of our dear state is being decided. The time to participate, to take a stand and to take our destiny in our own hands is now,” Joseph said. item.title: Court dismisses case against man who allegedly threatened Kano governor
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Tuesday struck out the case filed against a man, Sanusi Dankaka, who allegedly threatened to publish nude videos and photographs of Gov. Abba Yusuf of Kano State via his Facebook page. Justice Salim Ibrahim struck out the case after the prosecution lawyer, A.Y. Afegbua, applied to withdraw the charge against Dankaka, the sole defendant. The defendant’s counsel, Kauna Penzin, did not raise objection to Afegbua’s application for withdrawal of the case, and the judge, in a short ruling, struck it out. Although Justice Ibrahim had adjourned the matter until Dec. 7 for commencement of trial after the defendant pleaded not guilty, the case was relisted on number 28, the last case on today’s cause list. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Dankaka was arraigned on a two-count charge, which bordered on cybercrime offences. The Department of State Services (DSS), in the charge marked: FHC/ABJ/CR/699/2026 and filed on Oct. 22 by Afegbua, accused the defendant of committing the offence in October 2026. In count one, Dankaka and some others still at large, in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau, were alleged to have attempted, via his Facebook page: “Sanusi Dankaka Yahaya”, to send out the malicious publication. He was alleged to have said that he possessed nude videos and photographs of Gov. Yusuf, “and threatened to release them to the public, and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 27 (1)(6) of the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act, 2015, as amended and punishable under Section 24 (1) of the same Act.” In count two, he and some others at large were alleged to have, via his Facebook page, “Sanusi Dankaka Yahaya”, sent out a malicious publication alleging that he possessed the said videos and photographs of the governor. The DSS said the content of the said publication, Dankaka knew was false, but was sent out for the purpose of causing annoyance, inconvenience, insult and injury to the person and reputation of Yusuf. The offence, the DSS said, is contrary to and punished under Section 24(1) of the Cybercrime (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act, 2015, as amended. (NAN) The post Court dismisses case against man who allegedly threatened Kano governor appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Insecurity gradually reducing in Nigeria – Kano Rep
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The member representing Bichi Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Abubakar Kabir Bichi, has said insecurity in the country is gradually reducing. Bichi said this on Monday during the inauguration of the Bichi chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council ahead of the 2027 general election. He acknowledged that Nigerians were unhappy with the security situation in the country but urged them to recognise what he described as gradual improvements. “People are not happy about insecurity, but it is gradually reducing. If you check the Kaduna-Abuja road, the insecurity has reduced,” he said. The lawmaker also called on residents of Bichi and Kano North to support President Bola Tinubu and the APC in the 2027 general elections. He argued that continued support for the president was important for the completion of ongoing development projects. According to him, many of the projects being executed in Bichi and other parts of Kano State depend on cooperation between the federal and state governments. “If you vote for me and don’t vote for President Tinubu, there is a problem. Most of these development projects are brought to Bichi and Kano through his consent,” he said. Bichi added that members of the National Assembly could not execute major projects without the approval and support of the executive arm of government. Also speaking, the Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, said Nigeria is gradually recovering from its challenges. Yusuf, represented by his deputy, Murtala Sule Garo, described the country as seriously wounded and undergoing a healing process. item.title: EFCC witness admits AMCON board approved NG Eagle sale
item.description: ₦149m proceeds paid into AMCON account with CBN, court told By Henry Ojelu LAGOS — A witness of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, on Tuesday admitted that the sale of NG Eagle airline was approved by the board of the Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria, AMCON, and that the proceeds of about ₦149 million were paid into the corporation’s account with the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN. The witness, Bawa Usman Kaltungo, made the admissions while being cross-examined by Olasupo Shasore, SAN, counsel to former AMCON Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Ahmed Kuru, at the Special Offences Court sitting in Ikeja, Lagos. Kuru is standing trial alongside four others before Justice Mojisola Dada over allegations arising from the management and sale of the airline. Under cross-examination, Kaltungo, the prosecution witness four, acknowledged that Kuru obtained the approval of the AMCON board, then chaired by Dr Amos Adamu, before the sale of NG Eagle. He also confirmed that the proceeds of the transaction were paid into AMCON’s account with the CBN. The admissions came after Shasore challenged the witness over his claim in the EFCC investigation report that AMCON illegally established NG Eagle and Super Bravo Limited. Shasore asked the witness to explain the basis for describing the establishment of the two entities as illegal, despite his more than 22 years of experience as an EFCC officer. “In your investigation report, you said AMCON illegally set up NG Eagle and another HoldCo called Super Bravo. Please explain to this court how they are illegal,” Shasore asked. In response, Kaltungo said the investigation relied on intelligence, including a Federal High Court judgment reportedly nullifying the sale of NG Eagle. However, he admitted that he was unaware, during the investigation, that the judgment had been appealed. The judgment was subsequently vacated and set aside by the appellate court. The witness also acknowledged that his memory could fail him, before conceding that Kuru did not make decisions without the requisite approvals of the AMCON board. The defence relied on the testimony to challenge the prosecution’s account of the transaction and its handling of the investigation. The EFCC had instituted the case following a petition by Femi Falana, SAN, on behalf of the promoters and shareholders of Arik Air. Those standing trial alongside Kuru include Kamilu Omokide, a former receiver manager of Arik Air; Captain Roy Ilegbodu, the airline’s chief executive officer; Union Bank Limited; and Super Bravo Limited. The trial is expected to continue on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. The post EFCC witness admits AMCON board approved NG Eagle sale appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kompany improving after collapse but no return date yet — Assistant coach
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany is improving after collapsing during training last week, but there is no confirmed date for his return, assistant coach Aaron Danks has said. According to Reuters, the Belgian was rushed to hospital on Friday after collapsing during a reserve-team training session. The 40-year-old had been battling a virus and had missed some training sessions in the days leading up to the incident. Danks, who visited Kompany on Monday, said the Bayern manager was in good spirits and appeared to be getting better each day, although there had been no major update on his diagnosis or return to work. “I paid him a short visit yesterday,” Danks told reporters on Tuesday ahead of Bayern’s German Cup second-round match against Magdeburg. “He is in good spirits. It looks like every day he is getting better. There are no major updates in terms of diagnosis or return to work. Let him rest, let him take his time,” he added. Bayern face a demanding run of fixtures in Kompany’s absence, beginning with Wednesday’s German Cup tie against Magdeburg, followed by Saturday’s Bundesliga clash with title rivals Borussia Dortmund. The German champions will then travel to Spain next week to face Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. Danks said his conversation with Kompany was informal, adding that they avoided discussing football tactics. “We had some good conversations with Kompany but kept it away from football and specific tactics,” he said. “It was just a friendly chat and nice to see him and catch up.” The assistant coach also reflected on an emotional week for Bayern, with Kompany’s health scare coming shortly before striker Harry Kane won the Ballon d’Or on Monday. Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the prestigious award, following Michael Owen’s triumph in 2001. Danks said the contrasting events had tested the squad emotionally but praised the team’s unity in dealing with the situation. “For us, we are super professional. Full extremes of life in the last week. Joys and highs for Harry and the lows of the last days,” he said. “To get through these moments we had to rely on our chemistry, our team spirit and that definitely helped us,” Danks added. item.title: Lagos Assembly okays establishment of state police
item.description: By Ebunoluwa Sessou The Lagos State House of Assembly has unanimously supported the proposed establishment of state police following its consideration of the constitutional amendment bill transmitted by the National Assembly. The support was declared by the Speaker of the House, Mr. Mudashiru Obasa, during plenary on Tuesday after the lawmakers reconvened to consider the proposed amendment. The bill, titled *Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Act, 2026*, seeks to provide for the establishment of the State Police Service and related matters. Speaking after reading the relevant sections of the proposed amendment, Obasa said the establishment of state police had remained a recurring issue from the fifth to the 10th Assembly, with successive legislatures deliberating on ways to strengthen security and protect lives and property. He described the development as a step forward but expressed concern that some issues previously raised by state legislatures, particularly those concerning control and the relationship between federal and state police structures, had not been adequately addressed. Obasa said he was pleased that the proposal had received attention, expressing hope that further developments in the amendment process would give states greater control over their policing arrangements. He commended President Bola Tinubu for his commitment to democracy and democratic institutions, as well as the National Assembly, particularly the Senate and the House of Representatives, for their contributions to the constitutional amendment process. The Speaker also commended state Houses of Assembly for supporting the proposal, noting that nearly 25 states had expressed support for the constitutional alteration. However, he stressed the need for clear constitutional provisions defining the functions and responsibilities of state police, warning that disparities in the proposed arrangements could create an imbalance between the federal and state governments. He also called for the establishment of parliamentary police to protect legislative institutions and preserve their independence. Citing past incidents in which state legislative buildings were allegedly demolished or locked up at the instance of governors, Obasa said dedicated parliamentary police would help prevent such occurrences, strengthen state legislatures and safeguard democratic institutions. He expressed confidence that the outstanding concerns would be addressed as the amendment process progressed. Obasa thanked his colleagues for supporting the proposal and urged continued cooperation between the state legislature and the National Assembly to ensure that the remaining issues were resolved. The House subsequently adjourned plenary until November 9, 2026. The post Lagos Assembly okays establishment of state police appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NCDC dismisses Ebola rumours, says no confirmed case in Nigeria
item.description: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has dismissed rumours linking the Ebola outbreak to a possible election postponement, saying Nigeria currently has no confirmed cases. The NCDC Director-General, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this at a virtual capacity-building workshop for journalists on effective Ebola reporting on Tuesday in Lagos, warning against misinformation that could undermine containment efforts. Idris said that 54 primary contacts linked to a woman evacuated to Switzerland remained under daily surveillance, in spite of three contacts who developed symptoms last week testing negative for Ebola. He cautioned that the absence of a confirmed case did not mean Nigeria had been declared Ebola-free, stressing that surveillance and contact tracing must continue until the authorities establish that no further transmission has occurred. “The fact that we currently have no confirmed case does not mean we should declare Nigeria Ebola-free. “We must continue surveillance and ensure that all contacts are properly monitored,” he said. The NCDC boss explained that the woman, whose infection was confirmed on Oct. 20 after she returned to Abuja from Uganda, was evacuated to Switzerland on Oct. 26 alongside her husband at the Swiss Government’s request and expense. He said the patient had improved clinically before her departure, adding that her evacuation should not be interpreted as a vote of no confidence in Nigeria’s healthcare system. Idris said that most of the 54 contacts were quarantined in Abuja, while a few observed self-quarantine at home, adding that surveillance also involved identifying secondary contacts who might have interacted with them. “Three contacts developed symptoms and were tested, but all returned negative results. “However, we cannot stop monitoring them because the results are reassuring,” he said. The NCDC director-general also confirmed approval of ₦100,000 weekly support for quarantined contacts to ease the financial hardship associated with movement restrictions and encourage cooperation with public health authorities. He said the intervention followed concerns about the welfare of affected individuals, noting that the agency was engaging the Federal Capital Territory Administration on its responsibilities towards those under quarantine. Idris urged journalists to verify information through official channels, correct false reports promptly and avoid publishing details that could identify patients or contacts, warning that stigmatisation could harm affected families and healthcare facilities. He reiterated that Ebola spreads through direct contact with the body fluids of an infected person who is sick, not through the air. He advised anyone experiencing fever with relevant travel or contact history to call the designated response hotline, 6232, before visiting a healthcare facility. (NAN) The post NCDC dismisses Ebola rumours, says no confirmed case in Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

need to tackle insecurity, strengthen local intelligence gathering and create employment opportunities for youths. ‎ ‎Speaker of the House, Aliyu Umar Yusuf, announced the decision on Tuesday during towards strengthening the country’s security architecture, noting that the growing threats to lives and property required more effective and responsive policing mechanisms. ‎ ‎He identified terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, farmer-herder clashes, political thuggery and other criminal activities as persistent security challenges that had made the need for decentralised policing increasingly urgent. ‎ ‎According to the Speaker, allowing states to establish their own police formations would enable them to respond more quickly to security threats within their jurisdictions. ‎ ‎He explained that state Assembly before being transmitted to state Houses of Assembly for consideration in line with Section 9 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. ‎ ‎The Speaker said the proposed arrangement would enable state governments to recruit personnel familiar with their communities, thereby improving responses to distress calls and complementing the operations of the Nigeria Police Force. ‎ ‎He added that decentralising policing could reduce administrative delays and improve operational efficiency, particularly in communities where urgent security interventions were required. ‎ ‎Beyond security, Yusuf item.title: 2027: Wike says PDP members across states must support Tinubu
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Minister of the Federal Capital Territory Nyesom Wike says he and the Peoples Democratic Party’s National Working Committee have agreed that PDP members in all states must support President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election. Wike made the statement on Tuesday in Rivers State during the unveiling of the Rainbow Coalition’s preferred candidates for the 2027 elections, saying the agreement reflected his position as PDP national leader and the support of the party’s NWC. “What this means is that as the National Leader of the People’s Democratic Party and with the support of the National Working Committee, we have agreed that all the states will support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” Wike said. He added that PDP members in several states must support Tinubu, as the Rainbow Coalition aims to unite people across party lines behind the president’s re-election bid. “So, every PDP member in Imo State, you will support Bola Ahmed Tinubu; every PDP member in Kwara, Gombe, Zamfara, Ogun, and all other states must support Bola Ahmed Tinubu as the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.” Wike also said only the party officials he identified and himself could speak on behalf of the PDP, citing the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) recognition of Mao Ohuabunwa as chairman of the party’s Board of Trustees (BOT) and Abdulrahman Mohammed as national chairman. “There is nothing like a factional leader; INEC has recognised the Peoples Democratic Party led by the Mao Ohuabunwa as chairman of the BOT and Hon. Abdulrahman Mohammed as the National Chairman, and nobody can speak on behalf of the party except these two people and me, the National Leader,” he added. The coalition unveiled its preferred candidates for the 2027 elections in Rivers, including Kingsley Chinda as its governorship candidate. Rainbow Coalition means no harm, meant to support Tinubu—Wike says, as he calls for united Rivers. Wike also said the Rainbow Coalition was formed to bring people from different political parties together in support of Tinubu. He thanked those who had agreed to work together under the coalition, including the APC governorship candidate, Kingsley Chinda, whom he named as a point of contact. “The candidate of the Rainbow Coalition, let me use as a point of contact, the governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress, to appreciate and thank all of you who have agreed to work together, who have agreed under the Rainbow Coalition to support His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, as the president of this country,” Wike said. He said Rivers State was united behind Tinubu and pledged that the state would not return to killings and political crisis. “For those who don’t know, they should know today that Rivers State is entirely for Tinubu. item.title: Chinese state TV suspends La Liga broadcasts after Mbappé remark
item.description: Chinese state television has suspended broadcasts of La Liga matches following remarks by Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe about Mao Zedong, state-owned China Media Group announced Tuesday. CMG, which oversees public broadcaster CCTV, said in a release that it had suspended the broadcast of La Liga matches, as well as advertisements involving the French player, following his comments in a viral video. The group said it had reached the decision on Monday, according to the statement. It also said that apologies from La Liga, Mbappe and Real Madrid were “an absolute prerequisite” and that nothing would be discussed until such apologies were received. Mbappe apologised in a statement on Tuesday, describing his comment about Mao as “ill-judged” and that he understood “it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world”. Spain’s La Liga also apologised in a separate statement, saying that it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans”. Major Chinese brands, including beverage giant Dongpeng, responded to the comments by dropping the France captain. item.title: ‘Wouldn’t be possible without you,’ Kane tells wife after Ballon d’Or win
item.description: By Emmanuel Okogba Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane has thanked his wife, Katie Goodland, for her support after being named winner of the 2026 Ballon d’Or award, declaring that his achievement “wouldn’t be possible without you.” He expressed gratitude to Goodland following the announcement, acknowledging her support throughout his football career as he celebrated one of the sport’s biggest individual honours. Kane, 33, had while receiving the award, spoken for more than 10 minutes, thanking his long-term partner, Goodland, and mother to his four children. “To my wife, Kate, my best friend,” Kane said. “We’ve been through ups and downs for sure. You’re my biggest supporter. I actually felt like you wanted this more than me myself. “The anxious wait for us to find out, I know it’s been horrible for you, here it is – we’ve done it! You always want the best for me, you sacrifice yourself to help me achieve my dreams, and I know they’re your dreams as well, so it wouldn’t be possible without you. “This is a trophy that we celebrate, not me. This is me and you, it’s all the family, all our close-knit team, so I just want to say thank you, I love you. “Can’t wait to enjoy this and celebrate tonight for sure. Love you.” The England captain enjoyed an impressive campaign with Bayern Munich last season, playing a key role in the club’s title-winning success and reinforcing his reputation as one of Europe’s leading forwards. He also featured for England at the recently concluded FIFA World Cup, where the Three Lions finished third. Kane emerged ahead of a final three-man shortlist that included France international Kylian Mbappe of Real Madrid and Spanish forward Lamine Yamal of Barcelona. The Ballon d’Or recognises outstanding individual performances in football, with Kane’s contributions at club and international levels placing him among the leading contenders for the award. Kane will now look to build on the achievement as he continues his pursuit of further success with Bayern Munich and England. item.title: Poverty normal globally, not created by Tinubu, says APC spokesperson, Morka
item.description: By Emmanuel Okogba Spokesperson of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Felix Morka, has defended President Bola Tinubu against criticism over poverty and hunger in Nigeria, arguing that successive administrations have failed to eradicate poverty. Morka made the remarks during a RIGHT OF REPLY on ARISE TV, Tuesday, while responding to questions about whether Tinubu was evading responsibility for the country’s economic challenges by describing poverty as a longstanding problem. “Poverty is something that is, you know, a feature of many societies around the globe. Poverty has been with us for a very long time,” he said. The APC spokesman cited the eight years former President Olusegun Obasanjo and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar spent in office together, arguing that they had also failed to eliminate poverty. “Now, in the historical context, Atiku Abubakar was vice president of the Federal Republic for eight years with the former president Olusegun Obasanjo. Now, between the two of them, they had eight years to eradicate poverty, assuming that poverty was that easy to snap your finger and eradicate. Now, let me quickly say that, you know, they didn’t eradicate poverty,” Morka said. He argued that other administrations had similarly failed to eliminate poverty, adding that the challenge could not be resolved simply by political declarations. “All of the other presidents who have come before them did not eradicate poverty, even if we were to suggest that they had a constitutional obligation to eradicate poverty, they didn’t. They couldn’t eradicate poverty,” he said. Morka maintained that Tinubu was therefore correct to refer to the historical context of poverty in Nigeria, rejecting suggestions that the president was using previous administrations to avoid accountability. “So when this president says poverty has been, and, you know, these individuals in their own term of office could have, you know, completely extinguished poverty, take it out. They didn’t. You know, he was saying something that was completely true and not controversial,” he said. He added that opposition figures, including Atiku, were wrong to criticise the president for referring to the past. “So it is only people who simply want to, you know, evade responsibility, like Atiku Abubakar, who will in fact say, you know, why are you referring to the past? Talk about the present,” Morka said. Defending Tinubu’s position, he added: “Listen, there’s no present without the past. The present is only the present because there’s a past, which this president was referring to. So that is not, you know, evading responsibility.” Morka also accused previous administrations of selling off Nigeria’s assets and leaving millions of citizens in poverty, although he did not provide specific details to substantiate the allegation in the interview excerpt. item.title: 2027: INEC chairman tasks staff on neutrality, security, operational readiness
item.description: …Says 13.9m voters in North-East must not be disenfranchised By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, has charged electoral officials across the North-East to uphold strict neutrality, strengthen operational preparedness and ensure that no eligible voter is disenfranchised in the 2027 general elections. Amupitan gave the charge on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at the North-East Zonal Interactive Staff Meeting and Operational Readiness Assessment for the 2027 general elections held in Gombe State. He said the credibility of the forthcoming elections would depend largely on the professionalism, integrity, punctuality and preparedness of electoral personnel at polling units, ward collation centres and local government offices. The INEC chairman warned that administrative negligence, logistical failures, partisan conduct and poor communication could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and provide opportunities for the spread of misinformation. According to him, the commission’s nationwide readiness assessment was designed to identify operational gaps, assess the preparedness of personnel and strengthen institutional capacity ahead of the elections. Amupitan explained that the North-East engagement followed similar exercises in the South-West, North-West and South-East geopolitical zones, adding that the commission’s leadership had undertaken physical inspections of electoral facilities in Gombe as part of its efforts to evaluate preparedness on the ground. He disclosed that the leadership had visited the palace of the Emir of Gombe, Alhaji (Dr.) Abubakar Shehu Abubakar III, CFR, and inspected INEC’s zonal store and Gombe Local Government Area office. He said the inspections were necessary to establish the commission’s actual level of preparedness rather than rely solely on administrative reports from headquarters. “The true integrity of an election is not determined in conference rooms in Abuja; it is forged in the field,” Amupitan said, stressing that the conduct of electoral officials at the grassroots would ultimately shape public perceptions of the 2027 polls. 13.9 million voters in North-East. Highlighting the electoral significance of the North-East, the INEC chairman disclosed that the zone accounted for 13,965,475 registered voters across Bauchi, Borno, Adamawa, Taraba, Gombe and Yobe states. The figure, he said, represented approximately 13.51 per cent of Nigeria’s registered voter population of more than 103 million. A breakdown presented at the meeting showed that Bauchi State had 3,012,547 registered voters, followed by Borno with 2,765,165, Adamawa with 2,431,146, Taraba with 2,254,380, Gombe with 1,768,566 and Yobe with 1,733,671. item.title: Reps move to tighten rules for EV, CNG vehicle imports, demand local service centres
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina,Abuja The House of Representatives has called for stricter regulations on the importation of electric vehicles (EVs), compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles and related equipment, proposing mandatory local maintenance centres, genuine spare parts and after-sales support for importers. The lawmakers also urged the Federal Government to establish a transparent licensing framework for companies importing alternative-fuel vehicles, warning against the risk of Nigeria becoming a dumping ground for vehicles without adequate technical support and safety safeguards. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by Rep. Ademorin Kuye during Wednesday’s plenary, where lawmakers raised concerns over consumer protection, vehicle safety, local investment and the country’s readiness for the growing adoption of cleaner transportation technologies. Under the proposed framework, the National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC), in collaboration with the Bureau of Public Procurement, Standards Organisation of Nigeria, Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies, would develop clear criteria for approving importers. Companies seeking approval could be required to establish certified service and maintenance centres in Nigeria, provide genuine spare parts and warranty support, and employ and train qualified Nigerian technicians. Other proposed conditions include investment in electric-vehicle charging stations or CNG refuelling facilities, compliance with national safety and environmental standards, and submission of consumer protection and after-sales service plans. The House also proposed a public register of approved importers and infrastructure providers to promote transparency and protect consumers. It stressed that the licensing process should be open, competitive and non-discriminatory, allowing all companies that meet the prescribed requirements to obtain approval. The lawmakers further called for tax incentives, import duty concessions and other fiscal benefits to be tied to compliance with the proposed framework to encourage investment in local infrastructure and technical capacity. Contributing to the debate, Rep. Dominic Okafor warned against allowing Nigeria to become a dumping ground for vehicles manufactured without adequate consideration for the needs of developing countries. He said importers must demonstrate their capacity to maintain the vehicles they bring into the country and provide adequate support to consumers after purchase. “It’s very important to see that all the players in this motion are dressed seriously, so that Nigeria is not made a dumping ground,” Okafor said. He observed that some manufacturers produce different categories of vehicles for Western markets and developing countries, including Nigeria, stressing the need for safeguards to ensure that imported vehicles meet local requirements. item.title: Mbappe Apologises For Mao Zedong Comment After Chinese Sponsors Dropped Him
item.description: Kylian Mbappe apologised on Tuesday after the Real Madrid star was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with state-run The paper reported that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from Spain’s La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photo-shopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. “My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset,” French forward Mbappe said in a statement in French, Chinese and English. Spain’s La Liga also apologised, saying it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga.” In China, jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976 — and whose drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths — remain taboo. Beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe consuming its sport drink, said it was terminating all cooperation with the France captain. “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” Dongpeng said in a statement. Bottles of Dongpeng Beverage Group’s “Bushuila” electrolyte drink featuring French football star Kylian Mbappe on the packaging are displayed at a convenience store in Beijing on October 27, 2026. (Photo by PEDRO PARDO / AFP) | PEDRO PARDO / AFP Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, and cheesemaker Milkground also said that they were cutting ties with Mbappe, who until now was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of social media followers. “Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo with 430 million views. One Weibo user said the “extremely serious wrong remarks… crossed the red line” and others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their bottles. Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said Mbappe’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people”.
